cs.t: I'm not a gamer but I bought an Acer gaming laptop. It's ugly, but powerful, and it was on sale. I've gotten used to the lights and angular features. Only annoying thing I can't remove is the logo which is some aggressive looking face thing. I'm happy with it but I get it that someone people just can't stand the aesthetics of gaming laptops. But they do have great perf metrics.
cs.th: Ask HN: What's your primary development laptop?

cs.t: I genuinely don't get these posts or the rhapsodies around framework. My 2012 HP 8570w elitebook is completely repairable and still going strong. The cheap Acer gaming laptop I've got has replaceable ram, ssd, NVME and you can even easily replace the screen. Even my boring HP G7 laptop is easy to get into and repair. I just think so much of the press and HN readers instinctively waste money on Mac's or the none Mac super thin equivalents that they don't realise repairable laptops from mainstream manufacturers never went away.
cs.th: Dell’s Bold Idea: A Laptop You Can Repair
